description: User Impersonation via Public Endpoint The public endpoint for user authentication may not properly validate user identity tokens or implement sufficient authentication controls, allowing attackers to forge or replay authentication requests. An attacker intercepts authentication requests, analyzes the token structure, and creates forged tokens to impersonate legitimate users.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1550 - Use Alternate Authentication Material
recommendation: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all user authentications

description: Privilege Elevation via Token Spoofing If token validation and identity propagation mechanisms are weak, attackers could modify token claims or attributes to gain access to higher-privileged roles. An attacker modifies the group membership claims in their identity token to gain admin privileges in connected AWS accounts.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1548 - Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
owaspTop10: A08:2021-Software and Data Integrity Failures
recommendation: Implement proper token signing and validation
recommendation: Implement least privilege access control

description: Unauthorized Access to AWS Organizations Without proper VPC controls and network segmentation, internal AWS Organizations endpoints might be accessible from the public internet. An attacker discovers and attempts to access AWS Organizations management APIs directly from the internet, bypassing intended access controls.
references: recommendation: Implement VPC endpoints for AWS Organizations

description: Identity Synchronization Failure Identity synchronization issues could result in stale or incorrect access permissions when users' roles or group memberships change. A terminated employee retains access to AWS resources due to failed identity synchronization between corporate directory and IAM Identity Center.
references: recommendation: Implement robust identity synchronization monitoring

description: DDoS Attack on Authentication Endpoint Attackers could generate a large volume of authentication requests to overwhelm the service and prevent legitimate authentication attempts. A distributed botnet sends thousands of authentication requests per second to the endpoint, causing service degradation.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service
recommendation: Implement AWS Shield and WAF
recommendation: Implement rate limiting and throttling

description: Insufficient Audit Logging Incomplete logging configuration could create blind spots in audit trails, particularly for IAM Identity Center events. An attacker performs unauthorized actions through IAM Identity Center, but the activities are not logged for later investigation.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1562.002 - Impair Defenses: Disable Windows Event Logging
owaspTop10: A09:2021-Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
recommendation: Implement log monitoring and alerting

description: Insufficient Permission Boundaries Without proper permission boundaries through RCPs and SCPs, users or roles could gain more access than intended through IAM policy modifications. A compromised admin account in a member account creates overly permissive IAM roles due to missing SCP restrictions.
